subject: Chemistry
title: Arenediazonium Salts: Diazotization, Sandmeyer, & Displacement Matrix
topics: 7. Diazotization of Primary Aromatic Amines (Ar-NH₂ + NaNO₂ + 2HCl at 0–5°C ──► Ar-N₂⁺Cl⁻)
Resonance Stabilization of Arenediazonium Salts vs Explosive Instability of Aliphatic Diazonium
7.1 Sandmeyer Reaction (Cu₂X₂/HX for Cl, Br, CN) vs Gattermann Reaction (Cu powder/HX)
7.2 Diazonium Replacement Matrix: KI (Iodine), Balz-Schiemann Fluorination (HBF₄, Δ ──► Ar-F)
Reduction to Benzene (H₃PO₂ or Ethanol) & Hydrolysis to Phenol (Warm H₂O at 283 K)
quickSummary: Arenediazonium salts (Ar-N₂⁺Cl⁻) are prepared by diazotization of 1° aromatic amines at 0–5°C (273–278 K) and are stabilized by resonance. Sandmeyer reaction uses Cu₂X₂ (higher yields); Gattermann uses Cu powder/HX. Displacement reactions: KI ──► Ar-I; Balz-Schiemann (HBF₄/Δ) ──► Ar-F; H₃PO₂ or EtOH ──► Benzene (Ar-H); Warm H₂O ──► Phenol (Ar-OH).
summary: Master diazotization conditions, Sandmeyer vs Gattermann mechanisms, Balz-Schiemann fluorination, and diazonium displacement reactions.

summaryBox.takeaway: Diazotization at 0–5°C (273–278 K). Sandmeyer uses Cu₂X₂/HX (higher yield); Gattermann uses Cu powder/HX. Proceed via aryl free radicals.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
SANDMEYER vs GATTERMANN COMPARISON
                       
   SANDMEYER REACTION:  $\text{Ar-N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- \xrightarrow{\mathbf{\text{Cu}_2\text{X}_2 / \text{HX}}} \text{Ar-X} + \text{N}_2 \uparrow \quad (\text{Higher Yields!})$
   GATTERMANN REACTION: $\text{Ar-N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- \xrightarrow{\mathbf{\text{Cu Powder / HX}}} \text{Ar-X} + \text{N}_2 \uparrow$
conceptBreakdown.content: Arenediazonium salts are synthesized by reacting aromatic $1^\circ$ amines with $	ext{NaNO}_2$ and $	ext{HCl}$ at $0	ext{--}5^\circ	ext{C}$. They serve as versatile synthetic precursors.

conceptBreakdown.title: 7.2 Diazonium Replacement Matrix
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
DIAZONIUM DISPLACEMENT MATRIX
                        
   1. Replacement by Iodine:      $\text{Ar-N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- + \text{KI} \xrightarrow{\text{Warm}} \mathbf{\text{Ar-I}} + \text{N}_2 \uparrow + \text{KCl}$
   2. Schiemann Reaction ($\text{F}$):   $\text{Ar-N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- + \text{HBF}_4 \rightarrow \text{Ar-N}_2^+\text{BF}_4^- \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathbf{\text{Ar-F}} + \text{N}_2 \uparrow + \text{BF}_3$
   3. Reduction to Benzene:        $\text{Ar-N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- + \mathbf{\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{Cu}^+} \mathbf{\text{Ar-H}} + \text{N}_2 \uparrow + \text{H}_3\text{PO}_3 + \text{HCl}$
                                  $\text{Ar-N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- + \mathbf{\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}} \longrightarrow \mathbf{\text{Ar-H}} + \text{N}_2 \uparrow + \text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{HCl}$
   4. Hydrolysis to Phenol:       $\text{Ar-N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{283\text{ K}} \mathbf{\text{Ar-OH}} + \text{N}_2 \uparrow + \text{HCl}$
   5. Reduction to Hydrazine:      $\text{Ar-N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- \xrightarrow{\text{SnCl}_2 / \text{HCl}} \mathbf{\text{Ar-NH-NH}_2 \text{ (Phenylhydrazine)}}$
conceptBreakdown.content: Review all functional group replacements from the diazonium intermediate, including reduction with $	ext{H}_3	ext{PO}_2$ or ethanol to regenerate benzene.

quickRevision: Sandmeyer uses Cu₂X₂/HX; Gattermann uses Cu powder/HX.
Balz-Schiemann uses HBF₄/Δ to produce Fluoroarene (Ar-F).
H₃PO₂ or EtOH reduces diazonium to Benzene (Ar-H).
